ORAL ORDER 1.
This Appeal is filed under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 read with Section 96 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908.
2. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1 The land of the appellants is situated at village Lakthar, Taluka Lakthar, District Surendrnagar, which was acquired for public purpose for G.I.D.C. Vasahat at Laktar.
The Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 was published on 03.05.1994 and Notification under Section 6 of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2024 undefined the Land Acquisition Act,1984 was published on 04.11.1995.

sentences.text: The Land Acquisition Officer, vide order dated 10.12.1997, awarded the compensation at the rate of Rs.21,500/- per hectare i.e. Rs.2.15/- per sq. mtr.

The claimants demanded Rs.50/- per sq. mtr. and challenged the award of the Special Land Acquisition Officer under Section 11 in the Land Reference Case No.1 of 1998 before the learned Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court No.3, District,
Surendranagar.

entities.text:
Fast Track Court No.3, District,
Surendranagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Vide judgment and award dated 03.04.2006, the learned Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court No.3, Surendrnagar passed an additional amount of compensation of Rs.17.85 paise per sq. mtr. in respect of acquired lands over and above, compensation which has been awarded to the claimants by the Land Acquisition Officer.
3.2 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order, the appellants-original claimants are before this Court.

4. Learned advocate for the appellants has submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2024 undefined the learned Presiding Officer has committed an error by mis- reading the evidence on record and has not rightly and properly considered the submissions canvassed before him.

It is further submitted that the reliance was placed by the original claimants upon various judgments and orders dated 20.01.2001 of the same village, Lakhtar passed in Land Reference Case Nos.306 of 1997 to 327 of 1997.

entities.text: Land Reference Case Nos.306 of 1997 to 327 of 1997
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is further submitted that against the said judgment and award, the State Government had preferred the First Appeal before this Court being First Appeal Nos.3067 of 2001 to 3088 of 2001.

entities.text: First Appeal Nos.3067 of 2001 to 3088 of 2001
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: This Court has confirmed the judgment and award order of the learned Reference Court, Surendranagar.

It is further submitted that the Land Reference Nos.306 of 1997 to 327 of 1997 of the same village, Lakthar was arising out of Section 4 Notification dated 02.12.1992, whereas in the present case, the Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 was published on 03.05.1994.

entities.text: Land Reference Nos.306 of 1997 to 327 of 1997
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

It is further submitted that the learned trial Court has not considered the 10% appreciation in market value while awarding the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2024 undefined compensation, i.e. 10%
appreciation for land in question for a period of 1 year and 5 months.
The learned trial Court, in Land Reference Case Nos.306 of 1997 to 327 of 1997, awarded an additional compensation of Rs.18/- per sq. mtr., which was confirmed by this Court.

entities.text: Land Reference Case Nos.306 of 1997 to 327 of 1997
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

It is further submitted that the learned trial Court has committed an error in not awarding additional compensation of Rs.20.54/- per sq. mtr.
instead of Rs.17.85/- sq. mtr. by considering the 10% rise for a period of 1 year and 5 months.

It is further submitted that the learned trial Court has not properly appreciated the documents produced at Exhibit-41, 42, 43 and 62.
5.
It is further submitted that the acquired land had facility of irrigation on the date of the Notification published under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984.

It is further submitted that the appellants used to pay water charges to the Irrigation Department and receipts were also issued by the said department which were produced from Exhibit-27 to Exhibit-30.
It is further submitted that the learned Presiding Officer did not consider the receipts in their real sense.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2024 undefined
Learned advocate for the appellants submitted that the learned Presiding Officer has committed an error of fact in considering the lands as non-irrigated lands.

sentences.text: The learned advocate for the appellants has further submitted that the claim which was put before the Special Land Acquisition Officer was Rs.50/- per sq. mtr.
However, the Special Land Acquisition Officer did not consider the claim of the appellants and awarded Rs.2.15 paise per sq. mtr. to the appellants.

7. The original opponents appeared and filed their objections at Exhibit-18 and contended that the lands were acquired for public purpose and after considering the evidence on record, the award was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
The Land Acquisition Officer has estimated the market value as of year 1995, which is just, proper and reasonable.
It is also contended in the reply that the Land Acquisition Officer has taken market value from the year 1990 till the date of Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2024 undefined 8.

The appellants of Land Reference Case No.2 of 1998 Laljibhai Shamjibhai Patel has filed his oral deposition at Exhibit-44 in Land Reference Case No.2 of 1998 and witness Jignesh Narshibhai has filed his deposition at Exhibit-62.
From the impugned judgment it transpired that heirs of Jagjivanbhai Dayabhai Hansraj have not submitted any oral evidence.
9. Considered the submissions of learned advocate for the appellants and paper book.

The land situated in District Surendrnagar, Taluka Lakthar was acquired for the purpose of G.I.D.C., Lakthar and Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 was published on 03.05.1994.

Notification under Section 6 was published on 04.11.1995 and thereafter, the award under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 came to be passed by the Land Acquisition Officer dated 10.12.1997.
The compensation was awarded at the rate of Rs.2.15 paise per sq. mtr.

The appellants challenged the said award before the learned Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court, Surendranagar being Land Reference No.1 of 1998 NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED:
11/03/2024 undefined under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984.

The learned Presiding Officer, Surendranagar has considered the fact that the appellants, though their cases are that acquired lands were irrigated lands, could not produce any document on record to the fact that the lands in questions were irrigated lands.
The documents, which were produced on record to show that Laljibhai Shamjibhai Patel was paying charges for water to the Irrigation Department, are not a sufficient piece of evidence.

On perusal of the receipts Exhibit - 27 to Exhibit-30 it does not reflect,
the appellants were using the water for irrigation purpose for the entire year.
The said receipts stand in the name of Laljibhai Shamjibhai Patel and not in the name of Jagjivanbhai Dayabhai Hansraj.
Even in the abstract of Village Form No.7/12, there is no mention about the land being irrigated land.

The receipts Exhibit-27 to Exhibit-30, which were considered by the learned Presiding Officer,
reflects facility of water was given to Laljibhai Shamjibhai Patel only for monsoon crops.
The appellants could not produce any evidence on record that the appellants were taking crops in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2024 undefined winter season also.

Legal heirs of deceased Jigvanbhai Dayabhai Hansraj has not placed on record any documents to prove that deceased Jigvanbhai Dayabhai Hansraj was paying water charges to irrigation department for taking crops for the entire year.
Thus, there is no worth considering evidence on fertility of the land.

In the present case, the learned Presiding Officer has considered the nature of land as well as fertility of the land in question.

The learned Presiding Officer has also considered the decision of the learned Civil Judge Senior Division, Surendranagar, in Land Reference Case Nos.306 of 1997 to 327 of 1997 of village, Lakthar, which was confirmed by this Court.

sentences.text: After considering the oral as well as documentary evidence, the learned Presiding Officer has awarded just and reasonable additional compensation at the rate of 17.85 paise per sq. mtr.

The appellants could not point out any contrary material from the case papers, whereby this Court can interfere in the findings NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1595/2007 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2024 undefined of the fact.
Resultantly, I do not find any reason to interfere in the findings arrived at by the learned Presiding Officer, First Track Court No.3, Surendarnagar.
Resultantly, the present First Appeal is dismissed.
11. Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Court forthwith.
